subject: Leadership
content: Global leadership involves leading across cultures, countries, and international systems. Global leaders understand diverse perspectives, adapt communication styles, respect cultural differences, and address transnational issues (climate change, poverty, health pandemics, peace). Characteristics: cultural intelligence (ability to work effectively across cultures), global mindset (curiosity about other countries), empathy, patience, second language skills. Nigerian global leaders: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (WTO Director-General, first African and first woman), Akinwumi Adesina (African Development Bank President), Mo Ibrahim (philanthropist, cell phone pioneer). You can develop global leadership: learn about other cultures, study world history, consider international issues, practice foreign languages (French, Arabic, Chinese). The world needs leaders who can unite rather than divide.
summary: Global leadership: leading across cultures and countries. Characteristics: cultural intelligence, global mindset, empathy. Nigerian global leaders: Okonjo-Iweala, Adesina, Mo Ibrahim.

subject: Leadership
content: Organizational culture is the shared values, beliefs, and behaviors that shape how people work together. Elements: values (what matters: integrity, innovation, customer focus), norms (unwritten rules: how people treat each other), rituals (regular practices: meetings, celebrations), symbols (logos, office layout), stories (legends about founders or heroes). Strong cultures improve performance, attract talent, retain employees. Weak cultures cause confusion, low morale, high turnover. Leaders shape culture by: modeling desired behaviors, rewarding aligned actions, hiring for cultural fit, communicating values repeatedly, addressing toxic behaviors. Nigerian organizations: banks (customer service culture), NGOs (mission-driven culture), tech startups (innovation culture). You shape culture in your groups: class, family, sports team. Be the culture you want.
summary: Organizational culture = shared values, beliefs, behaviors. Elements: values, norms, rituals, symbols, stories. Leaders shape culture by modeling, rewarding, communicating.

subject: Leadership
content: Leadership ethics are moral principles guiding leaders' decisions and actions. Ethical principles: honesty (tell truth, even when hard), integrity (align actions with values, do right even when no one watches), fairness (treat everyone equally, avoid favoritism), responsibility (own decisions and consequences, admit mistakes), respect (value all people regardless of status, listen to dissenting views), transparency (share information openly, explain decisions), accountability (answer for results, accept feedback). Unethical leadership examples: corruption, lying, favoritism, bullying, taking credit for others' work, covering up mistakes. Nigerian ethical leaders: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (anti-corruption), Dora Akunyili (fighting fake drugs), Simi Nwogugu (educational integrity). Ethical dilemmas: Should you report a friend's cheating? Should you accept a gift that might influence your decision? Ethics requires courage.
summary: Leadership ethics: moral principles for leaders. Principles: honesty, integrity, fairness, responsibility, respect, transparency, accountability. Requires courage to do right.

subject: Leadership
content: The future of leadership requires adapting to rapid change: technology (AI, automation, remote work), demographics (diverse workforce), environment (climate change, sustainability), globalization (interconnected economies), social change (equity, inclusion, purpose-driven work). Future leader skills: adaptability (learn continuously, embrace change), digital literacy (use technology effectively), empathy (understand diverse perspectives), resilience (bounce back from setbacks), systems thinking (see interconnections), collaboration (work across boundaries), creativity (generate novel solutions), emotional intelligence (manage self and relationships). Nigerian future leaders: young entrepreneurs, tech founders, social innovators, climate activists. You can prepare now: learn coding, practice remote collaboration, study global issues, develop empathy, lead projects, embrace failure as learning. The best leaders will be lifelong learners.
summary: Future leadership requires adapting to change. Skills: adaptability, digital literacy, empathy, resilience, systems thinking, collaboration, creativity, emotional intelligence.
